correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in X give the exact conditional X-nullcline equation, and arbitrary antiderivative tests in Z give E[X|Z]=(k5/(k3 B))Z. Substitution turns each coordinate speed into a conditional residual, yielding the two mean-square defect identities by orthogonality. If either defect is zero, one of X or Z is constant on every support trajectory; the linear Z and Y equations then force all coordinates to be constant on bounded complete trajectories, so the support is equilibrium-only. The packaged checker verifies the polynomial decompositions and the historical parameter specialization.

originality.rationale: The complete foundational 1974 article was inspected and contains the model, stable numerical limit cycle, stiff two-variable reduction, and normal-mode stability calculation but no invariant-measure conditional regression or variance-speed defect. Later same-object sources inspected or compared focus on periodic waves, reduced-model bifurcations, global Hopf branches, or historical/model exposition. Nine semantic-index queries covering direct and equivalent formulations returned only analogues in other systems. The claim is restricted to the two conditional nullcline calibrations, their exact speed defects, and equilibrium-only equality classification.

value.rationale: The Oregonator is a canonical experimentally grounded chemical oscillator, and the 1974 source emphasizes strong phase-dependent concentration excursions and a stable closed trajectory. The accepted result provides parameter-explicit stationary diagnostics that are independent of phase parametrization: one conditional mean lies exactly on the nonlinear X-nullcline, the catalyst coordinate has an exact linear regression, and deviations from those calibrations are measured by coordinate-speed energies with complete equality classification. For the historical parameter set the catalyst law becomes the concrete calibration E[X|Z]=Z/480, making the result directly checkable on simulated or experimental stationary cycle data rather than a routine equilibrium recomputation.
